before.name: STAR kindergarten: small class assignment effect
before.description: Initial assignment effect on achievement relative to regular classes without a full-time aide. Standard errors account for within-class correlation; grade-level estimates share participants.

after.name: In Tennessee STAR, small-class assignment raised kindergarten achievement by an estimated 5.36 percentile points.
after.description: Compared with regular classes without a full-time aide, the estimated gain in average Stanford test percentile rank was 5.36 points (class-clustered SE 1.21). Krueger (1999), Table V column 7, reports the effect of initial assignment, not a percentage increase in test scores.

locator: Table V, column 7, panel A, p. 512

before.name: STAR kindergarten: regular class with full-time aide assignment effect
before.description: Initial assignment effect on achievement relative to regular classes without a full-time aide. Standard errors account for within-class correlation; grade-level estimates share participants.

after.name: In Tennessee STAR, full-time-aide assignment did not clearly improve kindergarten achievement.
after.description: Compared with regular classes without a full-time aide, the estimated gain in average Stanford test percentile rank was 0.53 points (class-clustered SE 1.09). Krueger (1999), Table V column 7, found a statistically significant aide gain only in grade 1, not a consistent gain across grades.

locator: Table V, column 7, panel A, p. 512
